overview: COMPUTERRL introduces a framework for autonomous desktop intelligence featuring an API-GUI interaction paradigm, a distributed RL infrastructure for scalable environment simulation, and an Entropulse training strategy that alternates RL with SFT to mitigate entropy collapse, evaluated on OSWorld and OfficeWorld benchmarks.

modules.name: API-GUI Unified Action Space
modules.description: Defines the unified action space integrating conventional GUI operations (click, type, scroll) with dynamic API calls based on the currently active application. Manages the object-oriented representation of actions and the systematic parsing of the agent's Python-style pseudo-code outputs into executable environment commands.

modules.name: Automated API Construction Pipeline
modules.description: Implements the LLM-driven workflow for automatic API development, including requirement analysis from exemplar tasks, API interface implementation using Python libraries, and automated test case generation with error feedback loops for autonomous correction.

modules.name: Distributed Desktop Environment Cluster
modules.description: Constructs the scalable Ubuntu virtual machine infrastructure using qemu-in-docker and gRPC protocols. Manages multi-node clustering, centralized resource allocation, standardized AgentBench API interfaces, and web-based visualization for monitoring environment statuses and resource utilization.

modules.name: Multimodal Observation Processor
modules.description: Handles the construction of the agent's observation space by extracting accessibility tree data via pyatspi (element tags, text, coordinates, dimensions) and processing GUI screenshots (resizing). Integrates contextual metadata such as open window hierarchies, active application info, and action feedback into the model's prompt format.

modules.name: Behavior Cloning Data Curation
modules.description: Manages the trajectory collection pipeline for the cold-start phase, including initial sampling with multiple LLMs, outcome stratification (Fully/Partially/Unsolved), and task-oriented augmentation using stratified sampling from a model pool. Filters and aggregates successful trajectories to construct the SFT dataset.

modules.name: Asynchronous RL Infrastructure
modules.description: Implements the fully asynchronous RL framework decoupling rollout collection from parameter updates. Handles resource partitioning, dynamic batch sizing for the trainer, modular component isolation (actor, reference, critic), and off-policy bias mitigation through replay buffer size limitation and trajectory synchronization.

modules.name: Step-Level Group Relative Policy Optimization
modules.description: Implements the Step-GRPO algorithm, extending standard GRPO to the step-level. Computes step-level advantages by grouping all steps from sampled trajectories of the same task, and calculates the clipped surrogate objective aggregated over step-level advantages with KL divergence penalties.

modules.name: Verifiable Reward System
modules.description: Implements the rule-based verification functions that evaluate task outcomes. Assigns binary rewards based on trajectory success and action format correctness, providing direct, verifiable training signals without relying on Bellman equation propagation.

modules.name: Entropulse Training Strategy
modules.description: Orchestrates the alternating RL and SFT training phases to combat entropy collapse. Manages the aggregation of successful rollout trajectories during RL, constructs a diverse SFT dataset from heterogeneous policies, and executes the SFT phase to restore policy entropy before resuming the second RL phase.

modules.name: Benchmark Evaluation Suite
modules.description: Executes the evaluation protocols for OSWorld, OSWorld-Verified, and OfficeWorld benchmarks. Measures task success rates, step efficiency, and computes domain-specific metrics for office applications (Word, Excel, PPT) to compare against baseline models.

modules.name: Experiment Tracking and Analysis
modules.description: Monitors and logs training dynamics, including average rewards, entropy loss, KL divergence, PPO KL, average margin, and Best-of-N rewards. Supports the generation of training curves with confidence intervals and error analysis categorization (vision, multi-app, illusion).
